segments.text: All right, awesome.

Thank you, everyone, for being here tonight. This is a special meeting of the Board of Education for September 29,th 2026, is called to order. All items being considered this evening are posted on the PPS website under the Board of Meetings tab. This meeting is also being streamed live on the PPS YouTube page. Good evening and welcome. Thank you all for being here. The purpose of tonight's meeting is for the board to approve responses to the recommendations made to the board in the draft bond performance audit covering fiscal years twenty twenty four, twenty five, and twenty five and twenty six. Once approved, the responses will be shared with the bond auditors to be included in their final bond audit report, which will be received on October 6th. At the direction of Director Sullivan, the chair of the audit committee, the senior internal performance auditor prepared draft responses and sent them to us all for us to review. And support was also provided by our general counsel. This is our first opportunity to discuss this together. So let's start this meeting by putting on the table. Do I have a motion and a second to adopt resolution 7382, resolution to approve the board responses to the recommendations in the draft bond performance audit for fiscal years 2024-25 and 25 to 26.
So moved.

I'll second. Thank you. Director Split moves and Director Engelsman seconds. All right, so now we can start board discussion. First off, before we begin, just a couple of reminders. I want to kind of note, especially for anyone who's watching, that this is an extremely awkward process. As many of you know, our bond auditors have requested that the draft audit report remain confidential. However, due to board meeting laws, all our discussions need to be public, which means that it's very difficult to talk about a confidential document in public. And so this is really the first time that we've had been able to get together as a board to discuss and draft our response to the audit. Now, a couple reminders. Number one, the bond auditors have reminded us that they strongly request that we keep our discussion focused on the responses and not the content of the report to respect their confidentiality request, I believe it's a request. I realize that's less than ideal this evening, so I want to assure our community that the final report will be made public on October 6th, and the audit report will be presented by the external bond auditors at our board meeting on October 20.

Over the weeks and months to come, the report and its recommendations will also be discussed in the audit committee and also the bond accountability committee as well. In order to submit responses to the draft audit, however, by the auditor's deadline, which I believe is tomorrow, we're meeting today under these wonderfully unique and legally challenging conditions. Well, let's first start off with a proposition that we'll vote on all the recommendations as a single vote. We may discuss any of these recommendations individually if necessary. Again, this is the first time we've been able to meet together to discuss this. So let me begin by asking: are there any recommendations that any board member would like to discuss separately and individually.
Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes.

Okay, so that's going to change the order of operations here. What we're going to do is, similar to a consent agenda when all items are pulled for separate discussions, we'll discuss each recommendation in order one at a time.
And so let's start with well, I get my documents in order here. Let's start with recommendation four.
Sarah Juan, can I ask a question? Could we find out which ones are being pulled and then maybe we only have to talk about three separately instead of all is that an option?

Yeah, I just figure, I mean, as we go down in order and no one wants to just move on to the next one. Um, Are there any? So, with recommendation four, let's start with four. We'll do this in order as it's listed on the document listed in board books. Um any board member have any amendments, recommendations, discussion points, considerations? Uh please raise your hand. I'll call you in order. Uh let's start with Vice Chair Chase Miller and then we'll go to Director Slay.

Thank you, Chair Wong. I have alternate language for our response. I don't know. Seems like I'll just share it and we can talk about it. And it looks like Christy does also. So I don't know. I'll leave the process to you,

but I'll just. Yeah. All I was going to say is it seems like something we already do, but I'm happy to just say that and then let you suggest the alternative language. That's all I wanted to flag for people.
Okay, thank you.

My amended response is concur with comments. PPS Board of Education agrees the Office of Internal Performance Audit could periodically review the implementation of bond audit recommendations as part of its assurance function, the board will discuss the frequency and timing of any review and develop a process that includes feedback to the whole board. And I think the change between this and the original is really just us taking this offline to nail down the logistics and the planning of it, ourselves, having some conversation around it. Can you read that one more time? Sure. PPS Board of Education agrees the Office of Internal Performance Audit could periodically review the implementation of the bond audit recommendation as part of its assurance function. The board will discuss the frequency and timing of any review and develop a process that includes feedback to the whole board.
Can I? Board members, would it be helpful if you share proposed language with me? I think I have some of these. I could put them on the screen. Would that be?
Yes, I think that would be helpful. That'd be great. That's possible.
Roseanne, I have two, and I emailed them to you in a shared document.
All right, great.
Let's start with Director Engelsman, and then we'll move to Director Slade again.
Oh, I think I put my hand up last. I was just going to question why we're changing should to could before we go further.
Because the internal auditor could do this, but I am not.
I think as we discuss some of this more.

It could be that it could be that we decide that we want a contract for someone that does just bond audit-related stuff. And then, in that case, maybe we would want it to be that person instead of our internal auditor. So, it just leaves the door open for us to make the decisions that we need to make without being tied into binding language.

I appreciate that. I guess my concern, and I know we're not supposed to go into the document, but it's impossible not to. The bond auditors on page 22 suggest that we assign the board's Office of Internal Performance Auditor the responsibility to periodically review. They don't leave question about whether that is their recommendation, or whether we, who are neither bond auditors nor experienced in this process, should take time to do anything other than assign. So I like the idea, I like your second. sentence Okay, I'm not comfortable with changing it from should, which is a you must to could.
I'll just I think that assumes that we are going to concur with following recommendations and that they're going to go forward without edit.
Move on to Director Slate.

I don't feel particularly comfortable weakening the recommendation here. This is something we already do. Our internal auditor has already done for us. I was on the audits committee, and we spent a lot of time talking about past bond audits in that space. And so to me, I feel like this would mark stepping back from something that we already have a process and are already doing. I'm honestly just kind of surprised that we're tackling this one in this way. It just seems like it's like something we already do, and it seems to go pretty well. I understand that throughout the conversation today, there's going to be talk of potentially adding using bond funds, somebody that's doing bond audit-related work. So, I don't, but I don't understand why that person would be outside of the Office of Internal Performance Audit. I'd assume they'd be part of it. So I don't think we're necessarily saying that, like, one person, I think we're more saying somebody could or should do it. Um, so I, I guess, and I also worry about having us have to discuss the frequency and timing requires us to do that in a board meeting.

When will we do that? I'm just worried that this would lead to, instead of just our, we assign it to our internal auditor, she starts working on it with the audit committee and they get going on this work. I would way rather have that than have a delay while we figure out what we want to do and maybe not even take the recommendation using the word could. So, I feel pretty strongly that I would want to keep the existing language since it's something we already do. And I don't want us to step back from what we're already doing and weaken that.
Thank you, Director LaFort.
Director LaFort. You're muted, Virginia.

Sorry. And now I'm disappearing. Apologies. Yeah, I was just going to concur with Director Engelsman and Director Split. This is not an area where I would be looking to weaken any language. In fact, I had a note to actually strengthen it to Will periodically review, um, but from what I'm hearing, I mean, I could stick with should, but moving to could is uh for me, it's not on the table for me.
Um Vice Chair Chase Miller?

I think I could compromise around the could language, but it is something like I would like us to have a conversation as a board before just going into it. That said, I actually didn't realize that was something that happens through the audit committee, and I'm because I'm not on the audit committee. And so I'm wondering if Christy could speak a little bit more about that because if it is something that we already do, then I feel like the entire response should be different.

Yeah, I feel like the response on the left looks like essentially what has been happening. We last summer got handed like a: here's all the recommendations. There were a lot of recommendations from past bond audits that hadn't been taken and that were like in process. Um, my understanding was that um, our auditor, internal auditor, approached different committees and said, Hey, some of these are related to things that, like, we had some that were policy-related, and some that were facilities-related, some that were like audit-related, and some that were like BAC related, what bond accountability committee. And so we had a couple of check-ins during the year where we kind of went over the list, talked a little bit about where progress was being made, but it was also something that happened in other committees just because that was where it was more appropriate to have those conversations and involve those school board members that were more engaged on that particular side of the work. That's how I would describe it. And then staff would report to us. And actually, just in the last year,

under new bond leadership, I guess would be a good way to put it, there'd actually been quite a bit of progress made on finally implementing many of those kind of hanging out recommendations from past audits. So, progress was made in this last year with that system.
Thank you. Once you started talking about it, I understood what you meant, but I hadn't connected that practice to this recommendation.

Yeah. Yeah. I think I raised my hand too. I'll present my thoughts. I like one of the things I do like about the amendment is that it allows the, you know, as since the Office of Internal Performance Audit is an employee of the board. I think it's important for the board as the boss to consider the workload of OIPA, the capacity, where things can maximize effectiveness. And the thing I do like about having this time to discuss frequency and timing review is to have that conversation about how we'd maximize our effectiveness in terms of our oversight. One, I do appreciate Director Split bringing up that if the OIPA already does this, I think we should at least amend to say that they already do this, and then perhaps strengthen the wording by saying that the OIPA will also, as already says, develop an implementation plan as part of it. But I think discussing the frequency and timing of the review, I think I agree it should be a conversation with the board, especially since we're trying to maximize our coverage here. Director to pass, and then we'll go to Director Sullivan after.
Thank you, and give me just a moment to kind of get back here.

I had a comment also, yes, and that the practice is already in place. I think the question for me was: we did have the Office of Internal Performance Auditor kind of assigning the work, and we hadn't really established, I think this is the board's responsibility to assign the work. And so I think what could strengthen the work itself is to have an understanding of the process flow. The board changes over a lot, and our committee structures change, and sometimes they come and go. And I think it's important to have a person that would track this and be able to have the authority to distribute to the different committees, having the authority and the wherewithal within their scope of responsibility. So I think that the practice is already there. What's not there is a good way to do the follow-through and to have a single-point person moving the work through the system.
Director Sullivan.
Yeah, I agree with that.

The internal auditor set that up very, you know, took quite a bit of time to set up which committee might be the best to work on it, mainly because nobody was following through at all on audit recommendations and was hoping that would help. So she became sort of the person who probably could have followed up herself, but it just made sense to do it on different committees.
So I don't,

it doesn't matter to me too much how the wording is, as long as we know somebody is making sure that those get followed up and not just ignored. And I think last year we did make some progress. There's still some outstanding ones from you know way long ago that we still need to do.
Thank you, Director LaFort.
Director LaFort.

Sorry, I think I've never been on a Zoom before. I just think that the language that we have here is already covering off on these concerns. It says that the OIPA will develop an implementation plan and it will be presented to the audit committee for review and feedback, which means it would eventually, go to the board anyway. So, we're just saying, come up with a plan that we can react to. And I will say that the process that was developed this year, I appreciate that the OIPA took the initiative to create the tracker that the committee chairs had access to the entire year. I used it every month to start checking off some recommendations that have been made by the auditors. So it definitely is something that has been implemented, but it's up to board members to take advantage of it. But so I feel like this recommendation serves us up in a way that we're going to have to have formal, you know, formal buy-in. But I think, again, I think this is just to concur with the recommendation and say we're going to start formulating a plan. I don't think it's to actually create the plan.
Thank you. Vice Chair Chase Miller.

I mean, at this stage in the conversation, I feel like at a minimum, it should be updated to reflect that this is something that we already do. So, maybe a concur with comments. And I mean, I'm still interested in us having a conversation as a board. I think there are other things in here that we're going to need to like work through and talk about as a group.

But whether or not my amendment goes forward as written, I do think that there should be some amendment that addresses what we're already doing. I think it's important to kind of push back on the idea that we didn't have our stuff together and don't have processes in place. There are a couple of places in this where we do have training or processes or whatever, and so I think those things should be noted.
Thank you. Director DePasse?

Yeah, I think this is just an example of one of those things in the large, you know, two-year audit that was missed in spite of having multiple conversations with our auditor. And so I agree that this is one of those, and there's, I think, four of four or five in there that kind of fundamentally change the job description of the Office of the Performance Auditor. And so I think that begs a board conversation. If it's already happening, we should absolutely, amend it, and we should also schedule time to figure out if we want to change the job description to include this as a task that's to be done by Office of Internal Performance Auditing.

I love that idea, Michelle. Or director to pass, sorry. It's Arben, you're seeing first names. So I also just wanted to suggest maybe there's, you know, compromise, Christy. Here I am. Hi. Okay. Maybe we could say that the implementation plan will be presented to the board for review and feedback instead of the audit committee, and that might help perhaps. And then the other piece we could change to the PPS Board of Education agrees the Office of Internal Performance Audit and perhaps additional auditors or something, like some sort of like wiggle there on who does it down the road.

Does we could just say agrees the Office of Internal Performance Audit should continue to periodically review since that's already done. So we could just add that continue to, and then the board as the so that way we don't have to have us have a conversation to have somebody start to work on this, but then in the end, it comes to us for that conversation to happen and a final decision to be made as a whole board. So I just thought I'd throw that out there and see if that might garner interest.
Yeah, I'll leave it at that. I don't really know what we do from here, but there's my suggestions.

I think we'll finish discussion soon, and then I'll ask Vice Chair Chase Miller or Director Split if you have motion for an amendment and we'll move from there. So let's just kind of finish this discussion, Director Sullivan and then Director LaFour.

Yeah, I agree with Director Chase Miller about having a concur with comment, the comment being that we are already doing this and continue to do it. And I don't see any reason that bring it, say, bring it to the full board instead of the audit committee. That's just one more thing for the full board to do because the audit committee can report to the board. So just seems like it doesn't have to be a whole board thing, even though everybody on the board will be working on it if it gets assigned to your committee. So You're still muted.
God, what is wrong with me?

I just wanted to say I really like Director Split's recommendation of switching, will continue to periodically review. I think that is a great idea. And also, just wanted to say that I know we're not supposed to talk about the contents of the audit, but I do believe that it does mention this process in the audit.

All right, it does sound like we have some potential amendments. So let me ask. I'm just going to circle back to Vice Chair Chase Miller to ask: Do you want to continue with your original amendment, or would you like to propose a new one?

I think I was looking to propose a new, but I think I need to spend some time with this language. I wonder if, can we keep moving through maybe while I do some tweaking and then maybe come back to it? Or is that too confusing?
No, that's fine. We can move to another recommendation and come back to this one.

Can I ask a quick question? It looked like when the screen zoomed out that all of them are already written and in some central place, and it would have been great to have them even 20 minutes in advance of this meeting to look at rather than looking at them on the fly. It looks like they're all in a central spot.
So I wasn't even done 20 minutes before the meeting. I sent Roseanne what I had. I had to work all day. I got this in between meetings. I would have loved to give everyone more time with them. Sorry.
I can say the same. I just submitted my comments at six o'clock, literally. So, same thing, busy during the day.

Yeah, and I think that's just to reiterate. I think I want to reiterate that this is a very clumsy process because of our meeting laws and because of the request for confidentiality. So it has been in previous practice when things like this happen that we email any things that we want to bring up to our board manager so that they have the text that can post during our meeting. I do want to say I also am I really like Director Slitz's recommendation that to amend and change concur with comments and change the wording to should continue. I also want to add to Director Sullivan's comment about that, yeah, this I agree that this work should be done in the audit committee, but also, following policy, if there's any recommendations, that the recommendations are proposed and referred to the full board. So that's the only thing I would add. I do want to move through this conversation, move to, and then come back to this one later. Director Ford, do you have something quick or substantial to add?
Would it be possible for Roseanne to share the live link with us so we can see it versus just that may be a meeting slaw issue because if there's a link that we're all kind of looking at or editing,
then that's outside of the video recording of the meeting and may cause some issues.

But how about the materials that Ms. Powell has? Can those be sent out and put in board books so we can at least be looking at them. If there's a lull in conversation, we could be skimming over things.
Good question.
I'll ask. I mean, I think we can send those out.
Yeah. Just also know: I did also email Roseanne a couple amendments I would also like to propose.

So I'm being asked to just understand the three amendments that I received from you, Director to pass, and Vice Chair Chase Miller to put those into board book. Is that what I'm hearing? Or to send them out? I'm not sure what the direction is.
Let me ask our general counsel, Liz, if it is okay for Roseanne to email everyone the text.

It is. Yes. You just can't be working on editing, co-editing in a document outside a public meeting. But if you each have a copy to look at, the thing that she, that's fine. Right now, discuss in this meeting, but you can't be editing in a live document outside the meeting.
Liz, could we is, well, Roseanne, are you currently in a Google Doc? A Google Drive Doc?
Yes, I'm gonna go ahead and share it.
And I will. I think, yeah, you can just share it.
Yes, if you just take a second to get to that tab, and I will do that. And I will set it so that you are viewers. How's that?
Great, thank you. That sounds great.

Um, awesome. We will uh put post or sorry, we'll come back to recommendation four in a little bit. So let's move on to the second recommendation, recommendation 28. Again, the question is: are there any board members that have any proposals, discussion points, or amendments they would like to bring forward?
I see Director LaForte's hand up,
but I. Director Laforte and then Director DePass.

Yeah, I just wanted to strike the language. It says, however, the full implementation of this recommendation will depend on budget availability. I'd like to strike depend on budget availability. I don't think that's an issue with bond funds. So it reads a little bit like an escape clause, and I don't, that's not something I really want us to have in here. So I would love for it to read. Full implementation of this recommendation will depend on the hiring process because I can imagine that specialized skills like this might take a little bit. It might be hard to find somebody in a really short period of time, and we'll need to leave the hiring window open. So, that is my suggestion.
Director to pass.

Thank you. Yeah, for the recommendation 28, it's to again, this is one of those. I looked at these recommendations and categorized them in two different ways. Category A has to do with expanding the Office of Internal Performance Auditing. And then category B is really changing, kind of like suggests and makes recommendations to our board protocols. The expansion of the Office of Performance Auditing is a concern of mine, but specifically for recommendation number 28, assign the Office of Internal Performance Auditor responsibility for providing assurance that the methodology for reducing district costs from monthly Presidio bond management invoice invoice complies with contract provisions and controls in place are functioning. And I said, do not concur. While the board agrees with the direction of this recommendation, it needs further review of the capacity of the OIPA and the coverage that's already provided by external sources, that would be our bond auditor, and that would be, I believe, there are two sets of auditors looking at these particular audit. Board leadership would work with the chair of the audit committee to discuss potential recommendations and consultation with key stakeholders with the goal of providing systems of assurances of contract compliances and proper functioning of internal controls. I would also recommend that this be done by someone that has deep industry expertise. I don't think this is a traditional audit,

and when we're looking at controls for a bond program management, I think that it would be really beneficial to have someone that has that industry experience. I also thought that the board, we will be going out for bid developing an RFP for a new bond auditor starting this year. And I would recommend that the board contributes to the development of that RFP. For the future bond auditor, that would include anything that we want an external bond auditor to do, including what the recommendation is in here, to be added to that scope of work.
I just want to note for everyone that Roseanne shared a document that has the amendments as proposed by Director DePass.
One,

since I have my hand raised, I'll go next. I want to agree with that sentiment. I don't agree with striking that language about the budget. I want to note that at this time, committing to hiring someone is, I believe, somewhat premature because we have our bond audit committee, we have our OIPA, we have an external bond auditor, we also have a couple financial auditors, and I think it's important to have kind of robust discussion analysis about where our coverage is, where there may be holes, and trying to figure out where how to maximize our coverage, right? So, if we're hiring someone different, whether it be an external auditor or internal, trying to figure out, I think there needs to be an analysis done first in terms of where we can maximize our effectiveness, especially since we're talking about limited bond funds and committing to hiring another internal auditor for the life of the bond, right, for the next seven years. I mean, we're we could be looking at upwards of something like almost two million dollars. And when we're talking about two million dollars,

I mean, that could be the difference between whether you know a school gets a seismic update or not, and so I think we owe it to the public and ourselves to have a robust discussion and analysis about where we are strong in terms of oversight and where we have weaknesses and then figuring out the best course of action after that to make sure that we use this money as effectively as possible. Let's move forward to Director Splitt.

Are we supposed to have the document we're talking about shared just on the screen or just with us is fine? That's just a side question. And then, like, if I just mean like on the screen, but I'm just because it's not in board books, but whatever. Um, the other thing, um, thank you. I just feel like this is what we're supposed to be doing, I think, in my humble opinion. Um, so so I, wow, the cost comparison on like seismic just really reminded me of when I got yelled at for supporting climate change stuff once. But so I'm a little like, okay, I need to like think for a second. So, because I don't want to like say that having an auditor is more important than kids' safety, and I'm worried I'm getting set up here, but I do think that what is being flagged here is that we have a new system. And instead of us having an internal office, we have an outside contractor. And while I trust that their best interests are in line with ours,

I think we owe it to ourselves to have that work checked by somebody internally so that we make sure that we are crossing T's, dotting I's, all of that. There's recommendations throughout these recommendations that point to the need for us to have someone with that expertise internally, to map to in order to handle a lot of these recommendations. I think by saying that we are not sure that we think that that's important enough to hire a person to do that for multiple of these recommendations makes me really concerned that we're not taking the audit and the recommendations seriously. I think that when we have an auditor look at our programs and give us suggestions, I tend to think we should take them. And I know that that's a difference of opinion, perhaps, between me and other members of the board. But I do think that I would prefer that we concur with the recommendation. I think that there could be a place where we simplify it because right now it does have those like two phases and have more of a discussion on next steps. But I do think that I really don't want us, I don't know how we can have this discussion tonight until we settle that question on hiring of a second auditor because that underlies so many of the other recommendations. And so, coming in tonight and hearing likely there's organized, seems like there's organized, you know, an organized effort here to disagree with a lot of these things that I wasn't prepared for at all. I thought we would see the audit and all think that we should take it seriously and do the thing. So I'm a little surprised that there's pushback. So I'm just trying to figure out: like, how do we land this second auditor focusing on the bond question so that we can move forward.

Because if we're going to have this argument, it's like if we decide now we're not going to do it, we're going to just, I just, it feels like it creates like a pyramid, and we're just like removing pieces that will make it impossible to keep building the thing if we are going to decide now that the majority of the board doesn't want to hire a second auditor and take those recommendations, which there are multiples of seriously. So, anyway, I'm just putting it out there that I'm surprised. I don't really know how to land this, but I do think we need to figure out how to have that discussion because, if right from the beget-go, it's like we're not going to do the things that are recommended here because we don't want to hire the second person, I just don't know how we move forward.
Sorry.
Thank you. Director Ingelsman?

Thank you. I have to agree with everything Director Split just said. I also would say that I don't have concerns about growing our Office of Internal Performance Auditor. I looked on Multnomah County's staff, and it looks like they have about nine or ten auditors for a $4 billion, I think it's $4 billion dollars. At least that's what I learned in all of this county chair conversation budget. And I realize I use their budget because that's about the size of our bond budget right now from the 2020, some of the leftovers from 2017, and then the 2025, and then I hastily did math, and it looks to me that 2 million out of 4 billion is about 0.0005. So it seems like money well spent for me, given some of the concerns in the audit of some costs being put where they don't belong and having to go back from general fund, I would never feel comfortable with someone checking themselves. The whole purpose of an external auditor is to let's see, where did I just read something that I thought was very interesting.

Anyway, so the whole purpose of an external or an internal or external auditor is to check things. And much like checking your own work, your brain will miss typos that someone else will catch immediately. And so it's this idea that someone else is checking something. And while I want to agree that someone's interests and intents are in the right place, that's not our job as a board. Our job is to have oversight, fiscal responsibility. And so I don't have concerns about raising it. And I certainly don't have the wherewithal or the experience or the training to say that the suggestion number 28 by an external auditor, bond auditor, to assign the Office of Internal Performance Auditor the responsibility for doing this, that we should call that into question. So I, I guess agree with Director Split that if the idea is to say we shouldn't hire another auditor, then I don't know how we go forward either.

Sorry, I just want to do a quick check. Roseanne, the recommendation 28 looks like it's the same. I think it's misnumbered. I think that was for recommendation four. Do we have text for recommendation 28 for the amendment?

While Ms. Powell's looking at that, I just wanted to add the line that I was looking for earlier, and it's on the Multnomah County website. And it's one of the auditors, and she says that she believes audits are a powerful tool for improving government and the services that help people in our community. And that just really spoke to me, even though I looked at it quickly. And yeah,
that's all.

Yeah, I agree. I think audits are extremely important. And I mean, Multnomah County, it's not really an apples-to-apples comparison because they actually have an office that turns out completed audits. So I'm concerned about the capacity here. And I think from the amendment that I kind of quickly typed out, it said that we agree with the direction of the recommendation, but it needs further review. And I would say, yes, we do need an external auditor. And that wouldn't be somebody that is hired. That would be someone that has, again, industry experience that is able, that is not connected to the district, that is not connected to PPS that is that the board hires to do that check and those checks and balances. And so it's, I guess, a kind of a partial concur. I have a question. I also agree with what Chair Wong said about, you know, since I've been on the board, I think we've expanded the audit function,

not just internally, but the number of eyes on all of our work substantially. And we do need to understand, I'd like to understand personally where there are gaps in service. Where are things slipping through the cracks? Some of what's slipping through the cracks may be financial, that would be in a different office, but I do agree that an external and independent auditor looking over those controls that has industry experience would be helpful.
Director LaFort, and then Director Sullivan.

Yeah, I just wanted to go back to something Director DePasse said earlier about the RFP for the external bond auditor and just point out that that was actually issued over the summer. It's closed, and I believe the work has actually already been awarded. So I just wanted to clarify that.
